opportunities.title: Propose vulnerability identity key and lifecycle schema
opportunities.summary: ### Summary Inspect the committed Anchore JSON fixtures and propose a schema for tracking vulnerabilities over time. Specifically: what combination of fields uniquely identifies "the same vulnerability" across scans? Candidates to evaluate include CVE ID alone, CVE + package name, CVE + package name + version, and CVE + package + image. Write up the tradeoffs, pick a recommendation, and sketch the analytics DB table(s) needed to support first_seen / last_seen / fixed_at / ignored_at / cleared_at fields. **Tech notes:** The Anchore JSON schema is documented at the Anchore project site; worth skimming before diving into fixtures. The goal of this spike is a decision, not code — resist the urge to start implementing. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Written proposal (markdown doc in PR) covering identity key options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation - [ ] Proposed analytics DB schema with column types and rationale - [ ] At least one worked example from the fixtures showing how the identity key behaves across days - [ ] Reviewed and approved by Brandon and/or Matt before next ticket starts ## Bounty: $250 This issue has been selected for our paid contributor program. opportunities.title: reward-manager: refund_pool does not update total_deposited or emit an event
opportunities.summary: `contracts/reward-manager/src/lib.rs:558-590` zeroes the balance and appends an audit entry, but: 1. **No event is emitted.** Every other value-moving operation publishes one — `POOL_CRT`, `POOL_FND`, `ADM_WDR`, `RewardsDistributedEvent`. A refund moves the entire pool balance and is invisible to indexers. Off-chain accounting reconstructed from events will show the pool as still funded, forever. 2. **`total_deposited` is left stale.** `get_reward_pool:591` returns `total_deposited` alongside `balance`, so after a refund the pool reports having received N XLM and holding 0, with no `total_refunded` to explain the difference. `total_distributed` is untouched too, so the accounting identity `deposited == balance + distributed + refunded` cannot be checked by anyone. 3. **The audit entry mislabels the operation** as `PoolOperation::Withdraw`, the same variant `admin_withdraw_unclaimed:1080` uses. A creator refund and an admin withdrawal are different events with different authorization and different meaning; the audit log cannot distinguish them. **Fix** Add a `RewardPoolRefundedEvent`, track `total_refunded` in storage, and add a `PoolOperation::Refund` variant. opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
